animejs.name: Anime.js Animation Engine

rendering_constraints.notes: Anime.js lacks first-class integration with HyperFrames window.__timelines registration and would conflict with the established GSAP pipeline.

animejs.justification: BLOCKED: Redundant dependency. The repository standardized on GSAP 3 which provides proven, deterministic timeline management for HyperFrames headless capture. Introducing Anime.js creates cognitive overhead, dual timeline conflicts, and violates the repository's dependency minimization policy.

canvas2d-native.name: HTML5 Canvas 2D Rendering Context

licensing.notes: Native web standard supported natively across all modern browser engines.

rendering_constraints.notes: Canvas drawing routines must bind to timeline progress callbacks and use seeded PRNG (mulberry32) rather than unseeded Math.random.

canvas2d-native.justification: Approved core technology. Used when procedural particle simulations, field lines, or function plots exceed SVG DOM performance ceilings (>1000 nodes).

gsap-bonus-plugins.name: GSAP 3.13+ formerly-Club plugins (SplitText, DrawSVG, MorphSVG)

licensing.notes: The workspace gsap-plugins skill states all plugins are free since the Webflow acquisition. The licence text for the exact version has not been reviewed in this workspace.

rendering_constraints.notes: Requires upgrading from the approved GSAP 3.12.5 to >= 3.13; existing projects pin 3.12.5 and must keep working.

gsap-bonus-plugins.justification: Proposed, not adopted. The studio runtime (src/studio) already covers split text, stroke drawing and morphs between compatible paths with GSAP 3.12.5 core. Adopt only for arbitrary-shape morphs (MorphSVG) after licence review and an M2 benchmark.

gsap.name: GreenSock Animation Platform (GSAP 3)

licensing.notes: Verified for motion graphic video renders and digital media explainer productions. Standard license covers commercial usage unless end users are charged directly for software bundling GSAP.

rendering_constraints.notes: Must instantiate timeline paused: true and mount to window.__timelines['root']. HyperFrames steps time deterministically. Studio compositions load the vendored copy (_studio/vendor/gsap.min.js, synced with the runtime since 1.2.0); `studio.py validate` warns on any script loaded over the network.

gsap.justification: Approved core dependency. GSAP 3 is the foundational animation timeline engine for this repository. It guarantees frame-accurate deterministic stepping and integrates directly with HyperFrames capture without DOM thrashing.

html-css-native.name: Native HTML and CSS (DOM text, layout, clip-path, filters)

licensing.notes: Open web standards implemented natively in Chromium/Blink.

rendering_constraints.notes: Animate transform, opacity, clip-path and CSS variables; avoid animating layout properties. Never set CSS transform on GSAP-animated elements (HyperFrames lint gsap_css_transform_conflict).

html-css-native.justification: Approved core technology: every existing composition already renders HTML text and CSS layout through HyperFrames. Registered explicitly so text, mask and layout primitives can declare their dependency.

html5-video.name: HTML5 Video Media Element

licensing.notes: Native HTML media element supported natively in Chromium.

rendering_constraints.notes: Video assets must be pre-normalized via scripts/ingest-asset.sh to 1280x720 @ 30fps silent H.264. Must specify muted and loop attributes.

html5-video.justification: Approved core technology. Used for hybrid cinematic layering (Veo/3D background underlays) placed beneath vector SVG stages.

lottie-web.name: Lottie Web (Bodymovin Animation Player)

rendering_constraints.notes: Use SVG renderer mode with autoplay: false. Timeline scrub driven deterministically via GSAP anim.goToAndStop(playhead.frame, true).

lottie-web.justification: Experimental runtime for rendering declarative JSON vector animations generated via Text-to-Lottie or exported from After Effects. Validated in tests/prototypes/lottie/ rendering 120 frames in 10.7s at 1280x720 30fps with 0 dropped frames.

p5-brush.name: p5.brush (Standalone WebGL2 Build)

licensing.notes: MIT license verified for p5.brush runtime (Alejandro Campos Uribe, commit d56350a6).

rendering_constraints.notes: Requires WebGL2 canvas context. Must seed using brush.seed() and brush.noiseSeed() before drawing. Validated in tests/prototypes/p5-brush with PSNR=inf determinism across repeated headless Chromium captures.

p5-brush.justification: Experimental natural-media brush and textured stroke capability. Evaluated via standalone build (no p5 dependency) in tests/prototypes/p5-brush/. Rendered 120 frames in 6.9s (17 fps) at 1280x720 with bitwise deterministic output (PSNR=inf). Kept isolated from production dependencies pending formal explainer adoption.

svg-native.name: Native Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG 1.1 / 2.0)

licensing.notes: Open web standard implemented natively inside Chromium/Blink engine.

rendering_constraints.notes: Vector elements rasterize on GPU via ANGLE Metal. Highly performant when DOM node count remains under 500.

svg-native.justification: Approved core technology. Standard 2D vector format ensuring crisp, non-blurry line work, typography, and mathematical diagrams across 720p and 1080p outputs.

threejs.name: Three.js 3D WebGL Library

licensing.notes: Standard MIT license allows commercial use and modification.

rendering_constraints.notes: Headless Chromium WebGL context creation with ANGLE Metal on 8GB Apple Silicon risks exceeding memory budgets (>2GB) and frame-capture synchronization is unverified without custom RAF interception.

threejs.justification: PROPOSED ONLY: Candidate for true 3D spatial models. NOT currently approved for production because WebGL context management on 8GB Unified RAM exceeds the 1.5 GB memory budget and lacks verified HyperFrames timeline synchronization hooks.

The dedicated browser port is set to 9333 (`agent-reach configure browser-port 9333`) because a long-lived Chrome holds 9222. Bilibili and V2EX were removed on 2026-11-03. Do not add more channels, log in, or start its browser (`agent-reach browser stop` when done) while a render, QA or Kokoro job could run. word-per-beat-sequence.purpose: Turn a slogan, list of features or manifesto into rhythm; make each word land as an event.
word-per-beat-sequence.visual_behaviour: Full-frame card, one centred or left-set word in heavy type, often with a full stop; hard cut every 0.25-2.5 s; background colour alternates between paper, ink and one or two accents.
word-per-beat-sequence.mechanics: Hard cuts on a beat grid; per-word entrance (mask rise, smear, character drop, stretch) of 0.2-0.5 s with expo or power ease-out; no exits (the cut replaces the card).

decomposition.timing: Measured cut spacing 0.23-0.47 s (ref-92c22222a2 11.25-12.65 s; ref-1cbe55c987 10.52-12.00 s), about 0.33-0.5 s (ref-0bf0254a3d), about 0.4-2.5 s (ref-b97f9168c6). Readable minimum is about 0.25 s for one short word.

word-slot-roll.name: Word or number slot roll

source.description: Three inspected references swap one word or number inside a still layout with a vertical roll (a slot, an odometer, a list scroller with a focused item).

word-slot-roll.technique: One slot of a sentence or figure rolls vertically to its next value while everything around it holds still, so the change itself is the message (what varies, what stays).
word-slot-roll.purpose: Show alternatives, growth or a list compactly; keep a headline stable while its key word changes.
word-slot-roll.visual_behaviour: The word scrolls up out of a one-line window as the next scrolls in, with a slight overshoot; widths re-centre the line.
word-slot-roll.mechanics: yPercent step of a masked column with back.out(1.5) over about 0.5 s; optional width tween so centred lines re-flow smoothly.

decomposition.timing: One roll per beat; each entry held at least about 0.6 s.

failure_modes: Entries changing faster than reading speed
Different word widths jumping without fit

implementation.approach: Studio.type.roll(parent, items, {fit}).to(tl, index, at)

limitations: Per-digit odometers (each digit its own column) are not built in; compose several rolls

source.description: An inspected reel pushes the camera through a word on a tilted panel into the next space.

zoom-through-transition.technique: The camera flies into an element (a letter counter, a window, a dot) until it passes the lens, and the next scene is found inside it.
zoom-through-transition.purpose: Spatial continuity; 'going deeper' into a topic.
zoom-through-transition.visual_behaviour: An element scales up rapidly with ease-in until its interior fills the frame; the next scene settles from slightly enlarged.
zoom-through-transition.mechanics: Scale to 8-20x about an interior point with power3/expo.in; next scene from scale 1.15 to 1 with ease-out; brief overlap.

decomposition.timing: About 0.5-0.8 s.

failure_modes: Scaling text to 20x blurs or costs raster time; switch at about 6x
Transform origin not on a hole or dark interior shows a flash

implementation.approach: Scale the outgoing scene about the target point (transformOrigin from Studio.boxAt), cut at cover, scale the incoming scene down from 1.15. Candidate Studio.fx.zoomThrough.

chronicle.name: Chronicle
chronicle.summary: A slow camera over a surface (map, document, timeline) that stamps dates, pushes into a detail and dissolves to mark time passing. For history, biography and anything told as what happened in what order.

visual_job.viewer_leaves_able_to: Place the events in order, in place and in time, and say what led to what.
visual_job.hero: A surface the camera moves over: map, document or timeline.

use_when: The structure is chronological.
Places and dates carry the meaning.
Primary documents, maps or photographs exist or can be honestly recreated.
avoid_when: The film is about one person's inner arc (use storybook).
The past is only a backdrop for a technical or financial argument.

alternates.when: Recent history where sepia would feel false.

scene_grammar.formula: Date and place stamped on a surface with the first image already visible.
A map or establishing document, framed so the place is readable.
The timeline advances; each event is date stamp, place mark, one-line fact.
Slow push into the document or photograph detail that mattered.
Before and after on the same surface.
Numbers and human cost, set with restraint.
Pull back to the whole surface with the date range and source.

motion.signature: A camera over a surface: push into a detail, pull back to the whole, dissolve to mark time passing.
motion.continuous_layer: Slow push or pan on the surface with grain boil, so a held document is never a held frame.
avoid: Modern UI elements on period material.
Generated period imagery that is not labelled as generated.

rules.ending: Pull back to the whole surface with the date range and source; hold the bed, no ramp to silence.

anti_patterns.pattern: Narration over a frame that does not change for more than max_beat_gap_sec.
anti_patterns.why: Breaks the anti-laziness rule. motion-qa flagged 41 s of 70 (cloud), 44 s of 92 (fridge), 79 s of 98 (Korea) as static or low-energy. Plan one visual event per 2-3 s from measured onsets and give every scene a drift layer (Studio.space.drift).

anti_patterns.pattern: Ramping the bed to zero over the last seconds.
anti_patterns.why: Cloud's last moment measured 19 LU under the body. Land a soft thud and ring on the last visual event, hold the bed, keep the tail after the last word to 2-3 s.

anti_patterns.pattern: The same empty stage in most scenes.
anti_patterns.why: repeat-layout-dom fired in all three films (3-5 of 6 scenes). A recurring grid is fine when its state changes; vary the hero's position or scale between scenes.

anti_patterns.pattern: Generated or recreated period imagery presented as archive.
anti_patterns.why: The design profile requires licensed or generated imagery to be labelled as such.

reference_projects.note: History and storytelling; 105 s portrait on editorial-light.
Collage treatment of a dated event.

data-ledger.name: Data Ledger
data-ledger.summary: A chart or counter that draws itself at the speed the narrator says the figure, with the annotation landing on the word. For money, markets, costs and any story whose point is a number and how it moved.

visual_job.viewer_leaves_able_to: State how big the thing is, how it changed, and what it is compared against.
visual_job.hero: One chart or counter that the narration reads aloud.

use_when: The point is a number, a trend or a comparison.
The film can be told as a baseline, a change and a so-what.
Figures come from a source that can be cited on screen.
avoid_when: The numbers support a mechanism the viewer must trace (use systems-blueprint).
The figures are not sourced; an unsourced chart is decoration.

alternates.when: Very few numbers and a type-led treatment.

scene_grammar.formula: The largest or most surprising figure, counted up in the first second.
The normal: axis, unit and period labelled before any change is drawn.
Draw the line or fill the bars as the figure is spoken; annotate the inflection.
The same axis with a second series or benchmark.
Tie the event to the move with callouts on the timeline.
The number at human scale: per person, per day, equivalent to something.
Source and date range, with the chart still alive.

motion.signature: Data draws itself at the speed the narrator says it.
motion.continuous_layer: Axes persist with the unit and the period labelled; gridlines only at labelled values and kept faint; a value readout follows the data front; slow scale on the chart group.
avoid: A chart that appears fully formed.
More than one chart type in a scene.
Pie charts, dual-axis charts, or more than three related metrics at once.
A legend box: label each series on the line itself.

rules.ending: Close on the human-scale number or the source line, with the chart still moving.

anti_patterns.pattern: A hero grid or map where only a few cells change per beat.
anti_patterns.why: The detector reads the whole frame: Korea's tile grid changed 4-11% of the frame and was flagged idle. Add a second moving layer (counter, travelling dot, label sweep).

anti_patterns.pattern: A headline that restates the narration.
anti_patterns.why: Fridge headlines repeated 82-83% of the voice, which wastes the strongest text slot. Use it for what the voice does not say (the number, the contrast, the date). A caption band is a legitimate repeat.

anti_patterns.pattern: Narration over a frame that does not change for more than max_beat_gap_sec.
anti_patterns.why: Breaks the anti-laziness rule. motion-qa flagged 41 s of 70 (cloud), 44 s of 92 (fridge), 79 s of 98 (Korea) as static or low-energy. Plan one visual event per 2-3 s from measured onsets and give every scene a drift layer (Studio.space.drift).

anti_patterns.pattern: Illustrative data not labelled as illustrative.
anti_patterns.why: The accuracy half of the quality bar. Label constructed series and say when reports differ; this worked in all three recent films.

anti_patterns.pattern: Axis without a unit, or a period without dates.
anti_patterns.why: A chart that cannot be read from the frame alone cannot be fact-checked.
anti_patterns.source: Authored from the design profile and VISION.md; not yet render-tested.

anti_patterns.pattern: A pie chart, a dual-axis chart, or a panel of four or more metrics.
anti_patterns.why: A viewer has about three seconds per beat. Angles cannot be compared, two scales cannot be read together and four panels cannot be studied. Two or three related metrics side by side is the ceiling.
anti_patterns.source: hyperframes-creative data-in-motion.md (HeyGen, Apache-2.0), adopted 2026-11-05 via docs/short-form-lessons.md; not yet render-tested here.

anti_patterns.pattern: A bare number floating on an empty canvas.
anti_patterns.why: A figure with no visual weight reads as text. Pair every number with something proportional to it: a fill bar, a ring, or a shape sized by value.
anti_patterns.source: hyperframes-creative data-in-motion.md, adopted 2026-11-05; not yet render-tested here.

anti_patterns.pattern: Successive figures for one concept drawn in different visual spaces.
anti_patterns.why: Keep the space and the look and change only the value. A change of look should signal a new concept, not just a new number.
anti_patterns.source: hyperframes-creative data-in-motion.md, adopted 2026-11-05; not yet render-tested here.

anti_patterns.pattern: A legend box, or default chart-library output.
anti_patterns.why: A legend sends the eye away from the data. Label the series where it is drawn, and build the chart in SVG with the studio runtime so it draws itself at the speed of the narration.
anti_patterns.source: hyperframes-creative data-in-motion.md, adopted 2026-11-05; not yet render-tested here.

news-brief.name: News Brief
news-brief.summary: An evidence board in which every claim carries its state: confirmed claims are solid and stamped, unconfirmed ones are dashed and grey. One reusable object (map, tile grid, timeline) changes state across the film.

visual_job.viewer_leaves_able_to: Say what happened, what is confirmed, what is not, and what to watch next.
visual_job.hero: A map, tile grid or timeline with a visible confidence state per claim.

use_when: An event is recent or still developing.
Sources disagree or part of the story is unconfirmed.
The film is short-form and portrait.
avoid_when: The event is settled history (use chronicle).
The story is a feeling rather than a set of claims (use storybook).

alternates.when: Illustrated treatment, as in the Korea and cloud films.

scene_grammar.formula: What, where, when stamped in the first second, with the hero object already on screen.
Confirmed facts one at a time, each with a source chip.
Map pins or dated ticks on a timeline.
How big: a counter or a one-cell-one-unit grid whose state changes.
What is not confirmed, drawn differently from what is: dashed, grey, labelled.
What officials or companies did, as dated steps.
The open questions and what to watch.
Sources and the 'as of' date; the picture still moves.

motion.signature: Evidence appears with its state, and one reusable object changes state across the film.
motion.continuous_layer: A drift layer on the hero object plus a second moving layer (counter, travelling dot, label sweep) so the whole frame changes.
avoid: Confirmed and unconfirmed claims drawn the same way.

rules.ending: Land a soft thud and ring on the last visual event; hold the bed; tail after the last word 2-3 s.

short_form.closing: Reel-length films (60 s or less): close on a word or image from the hook so a replay lands clean, then keep the soft thud and the tail above.

anti_patterns.pattern: Opening on a flat field.

anti_patterns.pattern: More than one ask at the end.

proof-canvas.name: Proof Canvas
proof-canvas.summary: One mathematical object built step by step and then transformed, with every variable keeping its colour for the whole film. For theorems, probability, geometry and quantitative arguments.

visual_job.viewer_leaves_able_to: Restate the claim and say why it has to be true.
visual_job.hero: A single mathematical object (lattice, curve, construction) that is constructed, then transformed.

use_when: The film builds an argument, derivation or construction.
A surprising claim is resolved by a visible key move.
Quantities are abstract (probabilities, sequences, geometry), not measurements.
avoid_when: The numbers are real-world measurements over time (use data-ledger).
The subject is a software or physical system (use systems-blueprint).

alternates.when: Equation-led film with almost no diagram.
The brief asks for dark (polya-recurrence used it).

scene_grammar.formula: State the surprising claim as a contrast between two objects shown side by side.
Define the object by building it from nothing; name each variable once and give it a colour.
Build the argument one visible change at a time; a variable keeps its colour and position throughout.
The key move: highlight, transform or collapse the object so the reason is visible.
The claim restated over the final state of the object, with the numbers.
What changes in the next case (another dimension, another rule), shown on the same object.

motion.signature: Construction, not appearance: each element is drawn or derived from the previous one.
motion.continuous_layer: The constructed object keeps running (seeded walkers, slow rotation, scale drift) so a held argument is never a held frame.
avoid: Decorative motion unrelated to the argument.

rules.ending: Restate the claim over the final state of the constructed object.

anti_patterns.why: Polya's closing scene had ~5.5 s of near-empty frame while narration continued; found only after the render. List every visual change time against audio/timeline.json before rendering, closing and quote scenes first.

anti_patterns.why: In the 12-bird swarm the returned birds were hidden under escaped trails. Draw the important minority last and thicker, and check a snapshot before the full render.

science-atlas.name: Science Atlas
science-atlas.summary: A specimen plate: one object shown whole, then opened up, with scale always visible. For structures, organisms, processes and findings in the natural world.

visual_job.viewer_leaves_able_to: Picture the structure or process at its real scale and name its parts.
visual_job.hero: One specimen shown whole, then cut away, with a live scale reference.

use_when: The subject has physical structure, scale or a process over time.
A study's finding is the payoff.
Orders of magnitude are part of the surprise.
avoid_when: The subject is man-made software or infrastructure (use systems-blueprint).
The finding is only a number (use data-ledger).

alternates.when: The brief asks for a dark, spatial or cross-section look.
Depth, night or space scale journeys (ocean-descent-documentary).

scene_grammar.formula: The object whole, with a scale bar from frame 1.
Zoom or compare through orders of magnitude, always with a unit bar.
Open the object: cross-section with labelled parts.
One variable changes over time; arrows carry the direction.
The finding as a before/after or chart, with sample size and uncertainty.
What the result does not show.
Back to the whole specimen at the starting scale, with the one-sentence finding.

motion.signature: Scale is always visible; objects are opened, not swapped.
motion.continuous_layer: Slow push or drift, plus seeded particles that follow the physical process.
avoid: A zoom with no scale reference.
Decorative particles unrelated to the process.
A finding stated without sample size or uncertainty.

rules.ending: Return to the whole specimen at the scale it started, with the one-sentence finding.
